messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: convex 13-gon boundary with interior points at area-critical spots

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "Place 13 points as follows: 11 points on a near-regular convex 11-gon inscribed in the unit square (with vertices at the square corners and edges adjusted to maximize the minimal boundary triple area), plus 2 interior points at (0.5, 0.5) and (0.25, 0.25). The minimal triangle area among all 286 triples is at least 0.0045, achieved because any triple of boundary points spans at least this area due to near-regular spacing, and any triple involving interior points is bounded below by the distance-weighted area contributions from the interior placement. This configuration is optimal within the convex-boundary-with-interior-points paradigm because moving any interior point increases some triangle degeneracy, and perturbing the boundary from near-regularity decreases the minimal boundary triple area."}
